idea-plugin.name: Duke Engine
idea-plugin.description:
Editor support for the files that hold a Duke Engine game's content: its .duke data files — its world, its maps, units, projectiles, effects, sounds. Duke Engine is a deterministic Java game engine; what a block may hold is read from the game's own records, so the plugin knows no particular game.

.duke files

  • Highlighting for block words, End, keys, values, numbers, strings, [a, b] lists and ; comments; brace matching and line comments
  • Every line of a block names a field of its class: Geometry = Cylinder with its fields under it, Modules = [ a block for each ], Armor for a map
  • Ctrl+Click from a key to the record component it fills, and from a class — a block's word or the class after = — to the Java class it is read as: Monster to its record, MoveUpdate to the module class, Cylinder to the shape
  • Keys and maps completed from the record the block is; after =, the classes the field may be, enum constants, Yes/No and asset paths; inside a list of records, the records it holds
  • Links between blocks, as the records mark them: Animations = Humanoid completed from the blocks there are, opened by Ctrl+Click and checked; clip names completed from the model and animation files a unit is drawn from, read out of the files themselves
  • Checked as the engine reads them: an unknown block or key, a value its type cannot read, a list where one value goes, a key written twice, a block with no End — each said in the engine's own words
  • A header written Monster Brute is fixed to Monster with Name = Brute inside
  • Asset and data paths, each written whole from the resource root, completed, checked with exact letter case, and opened by Ctrl+Click
  • Renaming a module class, a record component or an enum constant renames it in the data files
  • Folding for every block and every list over several lines, and a structure view of the blocks

A new game

  • File → New → Project → Duke Game writes a game that already runs: two units, a light and a camera as .duke blocks, a couple of the kit's effects with a unit wearing one, a Main that opens the 3D client, and a test that loads the whole thing headless

Duke Inspector

  • The block under the caret as a form, drawn from its record: every field with its default, grouped as the record groups them, each edited the way its type is — a number, Yes or No, a choice, a file, a link to another block, an animation clip, a colour, a nested record, a list of modules as cards — and its Javadoc as help
  • Every change is a line in the file: a default set is a line written, a reset is the line taken out, and Ctrl+Z takes back either
  • New from a template: a file with the record's own fields, listed in the game's file list
